acts.5.p1.b1.text: Now a man named Ananias, together with his wife Sapphira, also sold a piece of property.

acts.5.p1.b2.text: With his wife’s full knowledge, he kept back some of the proceeds for himself, …

acts.5.p1.b3.text: … but brought a portion and laid it at the apostles’ feet.

acts.5.p2.b2.text: … how is it that Satan has filled your heart to lie to the Holy Spirit and withhold some of the proceeds from the land?

acts.5.p2.b3.text: Did it not belong to you before it was sold? And after it was sold, was it not at your disposal?

acts.5.p2.b4.text: … You have not lied to men, but to God!”

acts.5.p3.b1.text: On hearing these words, Ananias fell down and died.

acts.5.p3.b2.text: And great fear came over all who heard what had happened.

acts.5.p3.b3.text: Then the young men stepped forward, wrapped up his body, and carried him out and buried him.

acts.5.p4.b1.text: About three hours later his wife also came in, unaware of what had happened.

acts.5.p4.b2.text: “Tell me, … is this the price you and your husband got for the land?”

acts.5.p4.b4.text: … Look, the feet of the men who buried your husband are at the door, and they will carry you out also.”

acts.5.p5.b1.text: At that instant she fell down at his feet and died.

acts.5.p5.b2.text: Then the young men came in and, finding her dead, carried her out …

acts.5.p5.b3.text: … and buried her beside her husband.

acts.5.p5.b4.text: And great fear came over the whole church and all who heard about these events.

acts.5.p6.b1.text: The apostles performed many signs and wonders among the people, and with one accord the believers gathered together in Solomon’s Colonnade.

acts.5.p6.b2.text: Although the people regarded them highly, no one else dared to join them.

acts.5.p6.b3.text: Yet more and more believers were brought to the Lord—large numbers of both men and women.

acts.5.p7.b1.text: As a result, people brought the sick into the streets and laid them on cots and mats, …

acts.5.p7.b2.text: … so that at least Peter’s shadow might fall on some of them as he passed by.

acts.5.p7.b3.text: Crowds also gathered from the towns around Jerusalem, bringing the sick and those tormented by unclean spirits, …

acts.5.p7.b4.text: … and all of them were healed.

acts.5.p8.b1.text: Then the high priest and all his associates, who belonged to the party of the Sadducees, were filled with jealousy. They went out

acts.5.p8.b2.text: and arrested the apostles and put them in the public jail.

acts.5.p8.b3.text: But during the night an angel of the Lord opened the doors of the jail and brought them out, saying,

acts.5.p8.b4.text: “Go, stand in the temple courts and tell the people the full message of this new life.”

acts.5.p9.b1.text: At daybreak the apostles entered the temple courts as they had been told and began to teach the people.

acts.5.p9.b2.text: When the high priest and his associates arrived, they convened the Sanhedrin—the full assembly of the elders of Israel—and sent to the jail for the apostles.

acts.5.p9.b3.text: “We found the jail securely locked, with the guards posted at the doors; …

acts.5.p9.b4.text: … but when we opened them, we found no one inside.”

acts.5.p10.b1.text: When the captain of the temple guard and the chief priests heard this account, they were perplexed as to what was happening.

acts.5.p10.b2.text: “Look, the men you put in jail are standing in the temple courts teaching the people!”

acts.5.p10.b3.text: At that point, the captain went with the officers and brought the apostles—but not by force, for fear the people would stone them.

acts.5.p11.b1.text: They brought them in and made them stand before the Sanhedrin, …

acts.5.p11.b2.text: “We gave you strict orders not to teach in this name,”

acts.5.p11.b3.text: … and are determined to make us responsible for this man’s blood.”

acts.5.p11.b4.text: “We must obey God rather than men.

acts.5.p12.b1.text: The God of our fathers raised up Jesus, whom you had killed by hanging Him on a tree.

acts.5.p12.b2.text: We are witnesses of these things, and so is the Holy Spirit, whom God has given to those who obey Him.”

acts.5.p12.b3.text: When the Council members heard this, they were enraged, and they resolved to put the apostles to death.

acts.5.p13.b1.text: But a Pharisee named Gamaliel, a teacher of the law who was honored by all the people, stood up in the Sanhedrin …

acts.5.p13.b2.text: … and ordered that the men be put outside for a short time.

acts.5.p13.b3.text: So in the present case I advise you: Leave these men alone. Let them go!

acts.5.p13.b4.text: But if it is from God, you will not be able to stop them. You may even find yourselves fighting against God.”

acts.5.p14.b1.text: They called the apostles in and had them flogged. Then they ordered them not to speak in the name of Jesus, and released them.

acts.5.p14.b2.text: The apostles left the Sanhedrin, rejoicing that they had been counted worthy of suffering disgrace for the Name.

acts.5.p14.b3.text: Every day, in the temple courts and from house to house, they did not stop teaching and proclaiming the good news that Jesus is the Christ.
